title: BugBountyScope
description: Structured scope + rules of engagement parsed from a bug-bounty program brief. Authoritative input to every pipeline stage; also used to filter findings in post-processing.

platform.description: e.g. HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti, YesWeHack, self-hosted

asset.description: repo URL/path, domain, API base, package name, etc.

out_of_scope.description: Assets, paths, or features explicitly excluded. Findings here MUST be dropped.

prohibited_techniques.description: Hard limits propagated into every prompt, e.g. 'no DoS / stress / volumetric testing', 'no automated scanning of live hosts', 'no social engineering', 'no physical', 'no testing against production data'.

severity_guidance.description: Program's stated severity model / what they care about / known-issue exclusions.

rate_limits.description: Any stated request-rate or testing-window constraints for live assets.

safe_harbor.description: Whether the program offers safe-harbor / authorization language.

automation_allowed.description: Whether the program permits automated tooling at all. If false, source-only static analysis only; never touch live assets with tooling.

reference_links.description: Docs, security pages, advisory history, architecture references to embed into generated prompts.

program_brief_raw.description: Original unparsed brief text, kept for audit trail and for the synthesis stage.

accepted_risks.description: Free-text description of intended / accepted-by-design security behaviors for this target (the vendor's threat model / known-limitations). Injected into audit + validate + corroborate so behaviors the maintainers consider intentional are not reported as vulnerabilities. Usually supplied out-of-band (--accepted-risks), not extracted from the brief.
